items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 4, 2026
items.excerpt: 04 November 2026• Update: 04 November 2026 Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Wednesday, including US Democrats projected to win both houses of Congress in midterm elections, US midterms delivering wave of historic firsts across states, and President Donald Trump’s pledging to end US financial aid to Israel by year’s end. Democrats were projected to take control of both chambers of the US Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, delivering a major political setback to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party, according to US media projections. The party made significant gains beyond its traditional strongholds, winning key races in states that overwhelmingly supported Trump in the 2024 presidential election, including Texas, South Carolina, Ohio, Iowa, and Kansas. The scale of the Democratic wave was still becoming clear early Wednesday, but the results pointed to widespread voter dissatisfaction with the Trump administration, particularly over the economy, rising living costs, and the president's decision to launch a war against Iran in February. - US midterms deliver wave of historic firsts across states, Congress Tuesday’s US midterm elections produced a series of historic firsts in races for governor, Senate and the House of Representatives. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor of any US state, as well as Georgia’s first woman and first Black governor. Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won in New Mexico to become the first Native American woman elected governor in US history, while Minnesota Democrat Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to the US Senate. In New Jersey, Democrat Adam Hamawy won the 12th Congressional District to become the state’s first Muslim member of Congress. Texas Democrat Gina Hinojosa became the state’s first Latina governor, while Republican Byron Donalds was elected Florida’s first Black governor. In Ohio, Amy Acton became the state’s first woman and first Jewish governor, while David Crowley became Wisconsin’s first Black governor. Illinois Democrat Juliana Stratton’s Senate victory also means three Black women will serve simultaneously in the chamber for the first time. - Trump pledges end to US aid for Israel by year’s end US President Donald Trump said Tuesday that Washington will stop providing financial aid to Israel by year's end under an agreement reached with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. "Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping, and they're fine with it because, you know, they've become a very successful country that are not in need, and we won't be paying any more to Israel," Trump told Fox News. He added that Washington would still provide assistance if needed, describing Israel as a regional partner with whom the US has maintained "a tremendous relationship," with Tel Aviv being the smaller partner.

items.title: Headlines for November 04, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Voters Deliver Stunning Rebuke of Trump with Democrats Regaining Control of Congress Nov 04, 2026 In a stunning repudiation of President Trump and his MAGA movement, Democrats regained control of the House and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Democrats have picked up at least seven Senate seats, winning races in Texas, Maine, Ohio, South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa and Kansas, as well as winning in Michigan. The Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska remain too close to call. In the House, Democrats have won at least 231 seats, with more races still to be decided. Only twice in the last half-century has control of both chambers changed hands in the same election. Democrats also clinched a majority of governorships. ## Historic Night in Texas as Democrats Win Senate Seat and Governorship Nov 04, 2026 In Texas, Democrats have shattered more than three decades of Republican dominance, winning races for U.S. Senate, governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general and even railroad commissioner. And Democrats are poised to possibly take control of the Texas House of Representatives for the first time since 2003. James Talarico will be the first Democrat to represent Texas in the U.S. Senate since Lloyd Bentsen left in 1993. Talarico spoke at a victory rally Tuesday night after defeating Trump-backed MAGA Republican Ken Paxton. ... Meanwhile, Texas Republican Governor Greg Abbott has lost his bid for a fourth term. Democratic state Representative Gina Hinojosa defeated Abbott by nearly 700,000 votes. She becomes Texas’s first-ever Latina governor. ... ## Progressive Michigan Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed Elected First Muslim Senator Nov 04, 2026 In Michigan, progressive Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed has defeated Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers in the race for an open Senate seat. El-Sayed campaigned on a platform of Medicare for All, ending military aid to Israel, and getting money out of politics. He becomes the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. ... ## Democrat Annie Andrews Wins South Carolina Senate Seat in a Stunning Upset Nov 04, 2026 In South Carolina, Democrat Annie Andrews has defeated Republican Senator Darline Graham by about 50,000 votes, out of 2 million cast. It’s a stunning upset in a state that Trump won by 18 points two years ago. Graham was appointed to fill the remainder of the term of her brother, the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, who died in July. Senator-elect Annie Andrews is a pediatrician from Charleston who opposes cuts to Medicaid and supports a public health insurance option.

items.title: US services sector activity cools slightly in October; inflation remains elevated By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 4 (Reuters) - US services sector growth slowed marginally in October amid a moderation in new orders, but supply chains remained strained, keeping prices for inputs elevated. The Institute for Supply Management said on Wednesday its nonmanufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index dipped to 54.5 last month from 54.9 in September. A reading above 50 indicates growth in the services sector, which accounts for more than two-thirds of US economic activity. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the PMI little changed at 54.8. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter on solid footing, though economists expect a slowdown in activity, with consumer spending expected to pull back after back-to-back quarters of robust growth. Spending is seen in part curbed by high inflation, which is eroding household purchasing power. Income at the disposal of households, after adjusting for inflation and taxes, fell in September after being unchanged in August. The saving rate is at a four-year low of 3.8%. The survey’s measure of new orders received by services businesses decreased to 55.9 last month from 59.8 in September. Delivery performance by suppliers deteriorated further against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Israel war with Iran and tariffs on imports. The Middle East conflict, now in its ninth month, has boosted energy prices and caused shortages of commodities that are shipped through the Strait of Hormuz. The survey’s measure of supplier deliveries jumped to 56.7 from 53.2 in September. A reading above 50 indicates slower deliveries. Deliveries have slowed for 23 consecutive months, keeping input prices high. The survey’s measure of prices paid by businesses for inputs eased to a still-high 73.0 last month from 74.0 in September. The ISM on Monday reported a slight moderation in prices paid for inputs by manufacturers in October. Economists expect inflation to continue to run above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target into 2027. The Fed last Wednesday left its benchmark overnight interest rate within the 3.75%-4.00% range while acknowledging that inflation "remains elevated." items.title: 2026 midterm election results: House, Senate live updates
items.excerpt: Democrats scored a seismic victory in the midterm elections, flipping both chambers of Congress from Republican control and setting the stage to challenge President Donald Trump's policy priorities from a position of strength. The Democratic victories spanning a surprising number of House districts and Senate seats mean the party will be able to launch congressional investigations with subpoena power. Democrats could eye the financial windfall Trump, his family members and his political allies have enjoyed since he regained the White House. They will likely examine the president's controversial, heavy-handed enforcement of immigration, his use of the Department of Justice to target people he considers enemies and favorable business dealings. ... Democratic Whip Katherine Clark of Massachusetts said the new Congress plans to pass legislation focused on affordability and rooting out corruption, key voter concerns that carried the party to victory. "We will pass legislation to lower prices, protect access to quality healthcare, and stamp out the corruption that has become a staple of Trump's Washington," Clark said in a statement. "We are ready to get to work." While the Democrats won a resounding victory, it is far from clear that they will be able to change policy in a substantive way when they take the reins of Congress in January. President Donald Trump told Fox News late Tuesday that he plans to use his veto power. "They'll send over things that are insane and I'll veto them," Trump said. "And after a couple months of vetoes, they'll call and they'll say how do we get this stuff done and we'll work together."

NEW YORK (AP) — Tony Butala, co-founder of the Grammy-nominated trio The Lettermen, has died at age 87. The band's media coordinator confirmed his death and shared a statement from the band expressing deep sadness and sending condolences to his family and friends. Butala died Sunday. Butala's career began in childhood, singing professionally by age 7. In the late ‘50s, he co-founded The Lettermen with Jim Pike and Bob Engemann.
